summary: Frontend-only auth UI test run for Wealth Coach. 11/12 flows verified end-to-end against the live preview URL. Signup validation (mismatch, duplicate email, valid->/onboarding), login valid+invalid, session persistence on reload, logout, protected-route redirect, forgot-password nav/submit->sent screen, reset-password no-token and mismatch all work correctly. One bug found: the inline 'Password must be at least 6 characters.' error never surfaces because the password <Input> has HTML5 minLength={6}, so the browser's native tooltip blocks submission before React's custom validator runs. Same issue on /reset-password short-password case.

ui_bugs.issue: Password inputs have HTML5 minLength={6}. When user submits a <6 char password, the browser's native validation tooltip ('Please lengthen this text to 6 characters or more...') fires and the form never submits, so the required inline React error 'Password must be at least 6 characters.' inside [data-testid=auth-error]/[data-testid=reset-error] is never rendered. Verified in test: signup_short_password -> error_shown=False.

action_items: Remove minLength={6} (and the matching attribute on confirm/reset inputs) from the password <Input> elements in /app/frontend/src/pages/Auth.jsx and /app/frontend/src/pages/ResetPassword.jsx so the React-level length check in submit() runs and the inline [data-testid=auth-error]/[data-testid=reset-error] message is shown. The JS length check already exists; just drop the HTML attribute (or switch to noValidate on the <form>).
critical_code_review_comments: HTML5 minLength conflicts with custom inline error UX — pick one validation layer. The spec explicitly expects the inline React error, so native validation should be disabled on these inputs.
Auth.jsx submit navigates to /onboarding or /app based on user.onboarded — relies on backend returning onboarded flag; works today but worth a unit test to prevent regressions.
ForgotPassword.jsx shows a generic 'If an account exists' message (good, prevents account enumeration) — matches security best practice.

ResetPassword.jsx: when token is missing, the form is hidden but the h1/subtitle 'Choose a new password / Pick something you'll remember' still render above the error banner — minor UX polish (consider hiding heading when !token).

context_for_next_testing_agent: After main agent removes minLength={6} (or adds noValidate), re-verify (a) /register with 3-char password shows [data-testid=auth-error] with text 'Password must be at least 6 characters.' and does NOT submit, and (b) /reset-password?token=abc with 3-char password shows [data-testid=reset-error] with same text (currently the previous mismatch error leaks through because form never submits). Everything else (login valid/invalid, session reload persistence, logout, protected route redirect, forgot flow sent screen, reset no-token banner, reset mismatch error) is already confirmed working.
rca of the issue: React form submit handler sets setError('Password must be at least 6 characters.') when password.length < 6. However, the <Input> components (shadcn Input -> native <input>) have minLength={6} + required. Browsers run constraint validation BEFORE invoking the submit handler; failing constraints raise an 'invalid' event and prevent form submission, surfacing the browser's own tooltip instead. Mitigation: remove minLength from the input, or set noValidate on the <form>, or call e.target.setAttribute('novalidate','') — any of these allows the submit handler to run and the inline [data-testid=auth-error] message to render.
